explanations: They first appeared 485 million years ago, at the dawn of the Early Ordovician, displacing the microbial and sponge structures of the Cambrian.
They occupy less than 0.1% of the world's ocean area, about half the area of France.
They are home to at least 25% of all marine species, and they flourish in waters that provide few nutrients.
Shallow ones are sometimes called rainforests of the sea, and form some of Earth's most diverse ecosystems.
It is an underwater ecosystem built by colonies of coral polyps, held together by calcium carbonate.

sources.excerpt: Coral reefs first appeared 485 million years ago, at the dawn of the Early Ordovician, displacing the microbial and sponge reefs of the Cambrian.
They occupy less than 0.1% of the world's ocean area, about half the area of France.
Yet, they provide a home for at least 25% of all marine species, including fish, mollusks, worms, crustaceans, echinoderms, sponges, tunicates and other cnidarians.
Coral reefs flourish in ocean waters that provide few nutrients.
Sometimes called rainforests of the sea, shallow coral reefs form some of Earth's most diverse ecosystems.
A coral reef is an underwater ecosystem characterized by reef-building corals. Reefs are formed of colonies of coral polyps held together by calcium carbonate.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: a sponge reef is named in the first clue as what these displaced; an atoll is one shape they take; a kelp forest is also called a rich marine habitat but is made of algae, not of polyps and calcium carbonate.
